awd_titl_txt: Conference: SAIL 2025: Summit for AI Institutes Leadership, Reston VA October 21-23, 2025
awd_abstract_narration:
This conference is the fourth annual program-wide meeting in the National AI Research Institutes Program. The Summit for AI Institutes Leadership (SAIL 2025) is an NSF-sponsored conference organized and executed by the program’s hub activity, the AI Institutes Virtual Organization (AIVO). The conference gathers the leaders and other key personnel from all AI Institutes to foster community building of those Institutes and other related activities into a network of collaborating organizations conducting knowledge exchange, growing their own competencies, and engaging with the broader public. The conference will take place October 21-23, 2025, in Reston, VA.

This conference aims to maximize the value of the AI Institutes as a flagship national AI investment. The conference delivers on the intent of NSF and its funding partners to continue to nurture the AI Institutes into a fully cohered national program, resulting in synergy across the constituent institutes that is greater than the sum of its parts. This gathering builds upon the successes and lessons from the previous SAIL events (2022 through 2024) and continues a successful record of establishing SAIL as the cornerstone event for the National AI Research Institutes program. The conference program addresses the needs of AI Institutes in various stages of their lifecycle, from those in their fifth year to newly established AI Institutes. This greatly enhances knowledge transfer among all. The program includes knowledge exchange about education and outreach, project management, computing and research infrastructure, communications, workforce development, and ethics. The conference is comprised of a balance of community-moderated panels with plenary sessions and other program-wide community building. A day of workshops prior to the main conference allows the program’s special interest groups to hold smaller community workshops around topics of interest withing a specialized area, and across institute boundaries. The plan also calls for an embedded activity for Institutes to showcase their technical accomplishments to one another and to a broader audience of potential partners from the broader community of public and private sectors, followed by the opportunity for prospective partners to network at the event toward greater understanding of funded research in AI and the potential initiation of new collaborations.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
SAIL remains the marquee event for the national AI Institutes. NSF AIVO reviewed conference survey feedback from SAIL 2024 and balanced it with feedback from SAIL 2023 to create a novel program for the fourth annual conference in 2025. With an eye toward continuously improving the value of the conference to member Institutes and the mission of their funding agencies, we engaged two new audiences in 2025 – graduate students/postdocs and Institute partners.

 

SAIL 2025 was held in Reston, VA October 21–23, 2025. The first day included SIG meetings and workshops, three of which were new:

 

  • Ed4AI – This session focused on education about AI at all levels, from K12 through workforce development. 

  • AI4Ed – This session was tailored for the five education-focused Institutes (iSAT, AI4ExceptionalEducation, INVITE, AI-ALOE, and Engage-AI).

  • Graduate Student & Postdoc Workshop – The workshop featured a poster session, student keynote address by Manikya Swathi Vallabhajosyula of ICICLE, and special sessions designed for the attendees’ career level. Students and postdocs provided 30-second videos about their research beforehand, which were shown throughout the conference. The 57 attendees were also invited to attend any of the general sessions, which were structured to demonstrate the leadership and collaboration among the Institutes community.

 

The main program was held October 22–23. Building upon efforts from SAIL 2024 to allow earlier-funded Institutes to share lessons learned with newer institutes and each other, the SAIL 2025 program emphasized growth opportunities, both with the Institutes community and through partnerships. In particular, the “Interdisciplinary Research Collaborations: Success Stories,” "Industry Collaborations: University Perspectives,” “Industry Collaborations: Industry Perspectives,” and “Leveraging AI Institute Collaboration for Advocacy” panel sessions emphasized the many ways Institutes are partnering to widen their reach.

Additionally, keynote speaker Robert Grey of Plug and Play, one of the most active investors and startup accelerators in the world, led an activity entitled “Building Your Collaboration” to help put the learnings into practice. Notably, the interactive session was well-attended by the graduate students and postdocs.

Other emphases for the general sessions included ethics, education and outreach, and workforce development. Cary Coglianese of the University of Pennsylvania delivered a keynote on management-based AI governance, and Alex Dimakis of UC Berkeley delivered a keynote on data curation for agents.

Looking back at the conference logistics, we note that the planning for each day, which required several months of detailed coordination with the hotel event planner and A/V staff, was key to delivering a well-executed event. A crucial process we will continue to implement well ahead of the conference is an in-person visit to the conference venue as well as assessment of room sizes and the A/V team and its capabilities.

This conference registration count was 312, which included 58 graduate students/postdocs and 12 partners. Forty-seven (47) conference attendees registered as remote attendees.
